description: Version 2 whole days, in the lineup.json case shape (see its description). settings may also hold: caps, {series, film}, present for rotation (defaults filled in) and for a capped shuffle, absent otherwise; runtimeFilter, {minMinutes?, maxMinutes?}, the runtime part of filters, applied to the epoch's pool with runtimeMs compared to minMinutes * 60000 and maxMinutes * 60000, both included; films, the film-to-collection map of the epoch (film ID to collection ID, already resolved), given only for rotation and a capped shuffle. An absent field means none. ordering.mode may also be rotation or inOrder. Every case has errorTimes S - 1 and E. Cases named 'v1 unchanged' are version 1 cases of lineup.json, copied unchanged.
source: Computed with an independent Python reference written from docs/rules-format.md only (version 1 and version 2: Groups in version 2, rotation, the capped shuffle, inOrder, Filters, Building the schedule, Primitives), without reading any Kotlin. The reference script is not committed, as for the version 1 vectors; it reproduces every case of key-order.json and lineup.json. Item IDs are synthetic.

cases.name: rotation, a short cycle wraps inside the day: the show runs from its tail into its head
cases.note: The cycle is about 7 hours, so the day plays it more than three times. At each wrap the show's last turn can meet its first turn (a cap exceeded at the cycle wrap, which the format allows).

cases.note: Continuous playout: the start run j is the run of the playout that contains S. The regular layout wraps from the last run of the cycle to run 0 inside the day.

cases.name: rotation, the planned end passes over a collection film: the rest of the collection is not eligible
cases.note: Planned end visits: ...00ab passed over; ...00ae placed; ...00b0 passed over; ...0004 passed over; ...0005 not eligible; ...0006 not eligible; ...00ac not eligible (it would fit); ...00ad not eligible (it would fit). Collection ...c0110009 holds films ...00ab (150 min), ...00ac (20 min) and ...00ad (25 min), in release order. Once ...00ab is passed over, its later films are not eligible, though at least one of them would fit; other items are still placed.

cases.note: minMinutes 1 is 60,000 ms (the default minimum runtime too) and maxMinutes 1440 is 86,400,000 ms (the epoch). Film ...00dd (60,000 ms) and film ...00df (86,400,000 ms) are in the pool; ...00de (59,999 ms) and ...00e0 (86,400,001 ms) are not. On this day the order starts with ...00df, which fills the day exactly.
